title: Water and Sediment Sampling to Discover Marine Bacteria
author: Karla Sofia Millan Lopez
materials: Make sure you have the necessary equipment to work on deck (overalls, suede gloves, helmet, safety booths, googles or sunglasses). Maintaining adequate hydration is crucial, as deck operations are quite exhausting.

When arriving at the sampling station equipments are deployed following the cruise plan. Each station is referred to by is geographical position and depth. The sampling operations were carried out aboard UNAM's Research Vessel Justo Sierra .
The equipment is recovered on deck and the next equipment in the sequence is prepared to be deployed.

Once the multicorer is retrieved and on deck, the equipment is secured before dettaching each core. If due to climatic conditions the sampling event was unsuccessful, additional sampling events are required in the same station an reposioning of the research vessel is needed.

When arriving at the sampling station equipments are deployed following the cruise plan. Each station is referred to by is geographical position and depth. The sampling operations were carried out aboard UNAM's Research Vessel Justo Sierra .

steps.title: Determine Seafloor and Site Characterization
steps.instruction: Determine the seafloor using a Kongsberg EM302 Multibeam Echosounder system. Deploy a SBE 9plus-Seabird Conductivity, Temperature, and Depth (CTD) profiler until it reaches approximately 50 meters above the seabed.

steps.title: Identify Water Sampling Zones
steps.instruction: Deploy the PNF-300 fluorometer (Wet Labs) to generate a fluorescence profile of the water column and identify the maximum peak. Remove caps from the fluorometer sensors before deployment.

substeps.instruction: Identify specific zones of interest based on depth measurements following site characterization.
Recover the fluorometer and replace the plugs on the sensors.

steps.title: Collect Water Samples
steps.instruction: Use a SBE 32 – Seabird Carousel equipped with 12 10-liter Niskin PVC bottles to collect water samples.

substeps.instruction: Descend the carousel with bottles open.
Remotely close bottles at predefined sampling depths (e.g., 1500m, 1000m, 500m, and surface).
Ensure the deepest bottle is closed first and labeled as 'bottom' and 'background'.
Stabilize equipment for a few seconds before acquiring samples; note that equipment is deployed/recovered at 1m/sec.
Record the time, coordinates, and bottle number in the electronic and physical logbooks.

steps.title: Recover and Process Water Samples
steps.instruction: Transport the carousel to the ship's deck and secure it.

substeps.instruction: Place hoses connected to the Niskin bottle nozzles into previously labeled 20-litre collection bottles.
Transport surface (~5 meters) and bottom (~3600 meters) samples to the on-board laboratory.

steps.title: Filter Water Samples
steps.instruction: Filter approximately 15 L of the sample through 0.22 µm Durapore™ PVDF Membrane Filters (Thermo Fisher Catalog #GVWP02500, 25mm diameter) using a PS reusable filtration unit (Wacol, 300-4000) and a vacuum pump (Millipore, WP6211560, 115 V/60 Hz).

substeps.instruction: Store saturated biomass filters in sterile aluminum foil wrapped in Parafilm.
Store one fraction of filters at 4 °C and another fraction in liquid nitrogen (ensure containers are tightly closed and secured).

steps.title: Collect Sediment Cores
steps.instruction: Deploy the multicorer to collect sediment samples, using cable tension to identify arrival on the seafloor.

substeps.instruction: Document and photograph each core upon arrival before detaching from the main frame.
Detach cores one by one and secure the top and bottom with rubber caps to prevent loss of sediment or bottom water.
Place identified cores in a core rack for transport to the processing area.
Clean the corers and multicorer to avoid cross-contamination.

steps.title: Process Sediment Cores
steps.instruction: Process cores in a cold room, lab, or on deck. Use non-plastic tools for plastic studies or non-metal tools for metal studies to avoid contamination.

substeps.instruction: Remove rubber caps firmly to prevent leakage or bubbles from bottom water.
Determine the required depth of sediment layers based on research objectives.
Cut layers using precut rings or sediment dispensers for uniformity.
Place each layer into a pre-labeled glass or plastic container/bag.
If required, retrieve the bottom of the core using an extruder.

steps.title: Subsample and Store Sediment
steps.instruction: Perform subsampling of the obtained sediment, potentially using hand-held syringes without tips to avoid perturbing layers.

substeps.instruction: Store one subsample at 4 °C in a glass container with a lid.
Store an additional 30 g sample in liquid nitrogen using sterile 50 mL Falcon Tubes (Fischer Scientific).

steps.title: Long-term Storage
steps.instruction: Store samples in an ultra-freezer at -80 °C (specifically -86 ºC using a NuAire NU-99728J) at the GLACIER institute laboratory.

substeps.instruction: Carefully recover samples from liquid nitrogen stores.
